definition: Estimating a continuous pain level from facial expressions or physiology — used in clinical and veterinary assessment.
details: Estimating a continuous pain level from facial expressions or physiology — used in clinical and veterinary assessment.

explainer.lead: Pain intensity regression is the estimation of a continuous pain level from facial expressions or physiology. It matters in clinical and veterinary assessment, where a graded measure is more useful than a category.

tiers.eli5: It is like reading a dial rather than a light switch: instead of saying 'in pain' or 'not in pain', it puts a number on how much.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build regression models over facial or physiological signals and predict a continuous score rather than a class. A pitfall is that pain has no single objective ground truth, so labels come from observer ratings and carry their noise.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is a regression task: a model maps features from facial expressions or physiology to a continuous pain level, evaluated with regression error rather than classification accuracy. The main limit is the reliability of the reference ratings used as targets.

explainer.example: A system takes a patient's facial video and outputs a continuous pain score, which a clinician compares against a bedside observation scale.
